The Long-Term Care Funding Checklist

What to write down, look up and ask about while Dad is managing on his own.

Download PDF

Dad is managing on his own and nobody is paying for care. You've started to wonder how the family would pay if that changed, and you know only pieces: a pension, some savings, a policy or two, the house. Check what you've done. Anything unchecked is something to get to when it suits you and Dad, not a verdict about him or about what he has.

Write down

Look up

Ask about

What this checklist doesn't do

It helps you write down, look up and ask. It doesn't say what a checked or unchecked box means, what care would cost, how long Dad's resources would last, or how Medicaid would treat anything he owns. Rules vary by state and change, so those questions go to your Medicaid planner or the appropriate licensed professional. Nothing here is legal, financial, tax or insurance advice.

Where this comes from

The kinds of income in the item marked 1 follow the list on LongTermCare.gov's Medicaid eligibility page. The item marked 2 follows Medicare.gov's suggestion to check a long-term care policy or call the insurance company. The rest come from the Medicaid Planning Roadmap's own working list for this step.
